transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (BlueWave ML Eng), Rina Desai (Platform Lead), Markus Klein (CTO)
Shared links: https://redwood.ai/pilot-catalog-comparison (sheet), https://redwood.ai/kv-priming-script (gist)

Auto-summary: (auto) Gating matrix review, validation of rollback and fallback behavior, agreement on canary percentages and timing; need for short rollback smoke tests and a final catalog note on pinned versions.

Topics:
- model selection tradeoffs (latency v cost)
- version pinning & canary strategy
- fallback routing and compatibility with cached KV state
- security/SSO checks prior to canary
- next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay everyone, hi, thanks for joining. The focus for today is quick: validate the gating and fallback behaviour for the pilot before we open the canary. We've got about 50 minutes.
[00:22] Tom (BlueWave): Yep, thanks. We're specifically worried about trailing latency spikes when we switch models mid-session, and like, how KV cache behaves if we roll back.
[00:35] Liam (Redwood SE): Right, good flag. We ran a simulated rollback last night where we did v1.2 -> v1.1 and kept the KV cache warmed. We saw a small mismatch in tokenization mapping, so some prompts had slightly different outputs, probably tokenizer version mismatch.
[00:58] Rina: Tokenizer mismatch, hmm, is that because v1.2 uses the new bpe merge? We can't accept regressions in the decisioning pipeline.
[01:10] Liam: It could be. The models in the catalog sheet list v1.2 as using 'bpe-x' and v1.1 as 'bpe-legacy'. I'll put that note in the comparison sheet.
[01:27] Markus (CTO): Quick question: if we do an automated fallback, does the request re-run from scratch or continue with existing KV? Because our session logic expects idempotency.
[01:42] Maya: Short answer: Redwood routing can either route to a compatible model variant that shares the same tokenizer and kv-format, or it can failover to a stateless variant which re-computes. For your workload we recommended compatible variant because of session continuity.
[02:04] Tom: Can you explain compatible variant? Is that the same as "model family" in the catalog?
[02:12] Liam: Yeah, model family concept — e.g., rwd-7b-quant and rwd-7b-ptq are compatible; they share tokenizer and kv layout so KV cache is portable. But if you switch family like rwd-7b -> rwd-13b, mem layout differs and we can't reuse KV.
[02:34] Speaker 1: (inaudible) 
[03:05] Maya: Let's run through the gating matrix we proposed: baseline latency SLO 200ms p95, cost delta threshold 15% and quality regression thresh hold 1.5 BLEU-ish metric on your eval set. If a new build exceeds these we gate it.
[03:28] Rina: About the BLEU number — our product folks want deterministic logic matches, not BLEU per se. Can we tie gating to your eval harness that runs our 150 golden prompts?
[03:45] Liam: Absolutely, we can plug your prompt set into Optimize and gate on exact-match plus soft similarity. We'll store the eval runs per version so rollbacks are traceable.
[04:12] Tom: When you say "store per version" is that in your console logs or in our VPC? Where does PII end up?
[04:24] Maya: Important Q. For dedicated & private we keep logs in your VPC by default. For hosted we retain minimal artifacts per your retention setting. We also support KMS-managed keys.
[04:41] Markus: We need to see the SOC2 + encryption notes before canary.
[04:48] Maya: We'll attach the security binder after the call, note action item.
[05:05] Liam: Back to rollback: in the bench we saw a 12% token-level cost improvement on v1.2 vs v1.1 but 40ms extra p95; given your 200ms SLO that becomes borderline.
[05:24] Tom: Right, so it's latency vs cost. Can the runtime do smart routing — like route non-latency-sensitive flows to the cheaper model and latency-critical flows to the faster?
[05:37] Liam: Yes, policy-based routing is supported; you can tag routes or URL paths. We also support runtime per-request hints so the client can pass "latency_priority: high".
[05:51] Rina: For the canary we want to start at 10% traffic for two days then go to 50% for one day, and then full if no regressions. Is that safe for rollback?
[06:03] Maya: That's a standard canary — we recommend doing an automated rollback window where if any of your key metrics spike we auto-revert to previous version. We'll configure thresholds together.
[06:15] Tom: What's the typical rollback time? Like seconds, minutes?
[06:20] Liam: The routing flip is near-instant. The slow part is clearing incompatible KV states; if we need to re-run stateful sessions some customers choose to drain in-flight sessions first. Practically, 30-90s to flip, plus however long session re-computation takes.
[06:39] Maya: Also note priming the KV cache for the new model reduces the cold-start regression. We've attached a KV priming script in the shared gist.
[06:52] Markus: Will priming cost a lot? We have budget guardrails.
[06:56] Liam: It's small relative to token cost, but depends on how many prefixes you prime. We can do selective priming — top 100 prefixes — and measure ROI.
[07:12] 
[07:40] (30 minute mark - mid-call notes)
[07:40] Tom: We ran your suggestion of selective priming for 200 prefixes, saw a 10% p95 improvement. However, on some multi-turn flows the outputs diverged when we fell back to v1.1.
[07:58] Liam: That divergence is probably due to the tokenizer mismatch we mentioned. For rollback compatibility we need to pin either tokenizers to the same behavior or restrict fallback to compatible variants.
[08:15] Rina: Are there automated checks to prevent accidental fallbacks to incompatible variants? We don't want silent degradations.
[08:24] Liam: Yes, the console has a compatibility matrix — you can mark variants as compatible/incompatible; routing engine enforces it. We'll show you the UI after.
[08:35] Maya: Also on the catalog sheet we added a column for tokenizer_family and kv_compat; Liam will populate specifics.
[08:46] Markus: One more infra note: our egress rules currently block outbound traffic to some regions. Will the canary be entirely within our VPC?
[08:59] Maya: For Dedicated it's in your VPC. For hosted, we can pin the region. We'll need your firewall rules so the runtime can reach the selected GPU pool.
[09:13] Tom: Ok. Now about metrics: We need to make sure the per-route cost numbers are understandable to finance. Can you produce a per-1k-token cost + projected monthly cost for our 5M token forecast?
[09:25] Liam: Sure, I'll add a sheet with cost at current quantization profiles and also run a 'what-if' for alternative batching.
[09:34] Rina: Also add an estimate for the KV priming run.
[09:37] Liam: Will do.
[09:55] 
[10:05] (10 minute break in transcript where some small chatter; timestamp jumps)
[12:01] Maya: Back on track. Let's outline the rollback smoke test that Redwood will run: 1) Replay 1k golden sessions on v1.2 with KV warmed; 2) flip routing to v1.1 and verify session continuity and QA metrics; 3) record diffs and err rates.
[12:22] Tom: For step 2 if mismatch occurs we want a captured diff set for manual inspection, not auto-silencing.
[12:31] Liam: Agreed — we will keep the diff artifacts in the shared bucket and include sample sessions with traceback.
[12:40] Rina: Will debug logs include prompt IDs only or full content? Need to avoid storing PII.
[12:48] Maya: By default we store prompt ID and hashes; you can opt-in to full content in a secure S3 within your VPC for debug, with KMS encryption.
[12:59] Tom: Good.
[13:15] Maya: Quick note: we also support a two-model policy where we keep prior version live as a cold fallback. That means if v1.2 fails we route to v1.1 but mark session as degraded and flag to ops. Downsides are extra cost and storage.
[13:33] Markus: That seems OK for the pilot but not long-term. We want to know exact cost impact before committing.
[13:41] Liam: We'll quantify.
[14:00] Maya: Any blockers on your side for the canary window?
[14:05] Tom: We need the SSO test user and confirmation of outbound egress rules. Also need the eval harness integrated into your Optimize tool.
[14:16] Rina: And we need the catalog doc showing which variants are tokenize-compatible.
[14:22] Maya: Action items captured. We'll attach updated catalog and security binder.
[14:36] 
[14:50] (closing, recap)
[14:50] Maya: Recap: Redwood to run rollback smoke test and share results by Friday (2025-06-13). SE to push updated catalog comparison with tokenizer_family and kv_compat columns. BlueWave to provide three golden prompt templates and confirm SSO test account by Thursday (2025-06-12). We'll schedule canary starting week of 6/16 with 10% initial traffic.
[15:18] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks.
[15:22] Rina: Thanks, all.
[15:25] Maya: I'll follow up with the binder and links. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription missed a couple names and technical acronyms (e.g., "KV" sometimes transcribed as "K V" or "K V cash"). There is occasional crosstalk.
